pass_a_gloss: [...] Christ bringing back the whole [earth] into the knowledge of the truth, and calling to conversion, and justifying in faith, and making glorious through sanctification, there was joy and festival among the spirits above? So, the heavens rejoicing that God had mercy on Israel, and not only, surely, on that according to flesh, but indeed also on that understood according to spirit, the foundations of the earth sounded the trumpet, that is, the sacred ministers of the gospel oracles; their sound piercing was carried everywhere, and as some sacred trumpets they cried aloud, announcing around the glory of the Saviour to those everywhere, and calling into knowledge of Christ both those from circumcision and those of old serving the creation beside the Creator. And foundations of the earth we say they have been named, for what cause? For Christ is the foundation of all and unshakable base, the one holding up all things, and holding firm toward well-being the things set firm; for upon him we are all built up, a spiritual house fitted together through the Spirit into a holy temple, into his dwelling place. For he dwells in our hearts through faith; and nearer foundations, and closer rather than we, would be understood apostles and evangelists, having become eyewitnesses and ministers of the word, and having become also for a support of faith. For having known that we must follow their traditions, we will keep the faith straight and undistorted for Christ. For it has been said somewhere by him to the divine Peter (when wisely and blamelessly confessing the faith in him he was saying: You are Christ the Son of the living God): You are Peter, and upon this rock I will found my Church, saying rock, I think, the unshakable [firmness] in faith of the disciple. And it has been said somewhere also through the voice of the one who sings psalms: His foundations in the holy mountains. And to holy mountains one must very well liken the holy apostles and evangelists, whose knowledge has been set firm like a foundation for those after them, not allowing those netted through them to fall over toward the counterfeit in faith. So the foundations of the earth sound the trumpet; but see the exactness. For Moses was thin-voiced and slow-tongued. For the law was not audible far, except to those in Judaea alone. But sound the trumpet, you who are ambassadors for the things of Christ. For their sound went out into all the earth, and their words into the ends of the inhabited world. And he has ordered the mountains to shout gladness; and the foundations of the earth, again calling them mountains in these; for the divine disciples are looked at and conspicuous, distinguished in deed and word, and to those everywhere kn[own] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …the whole earth to the knowledge of the truth, as Christ was bringing it back, calling it to conversion, justifying it by faith, and making it glorious through sanctification, there was joy and festival among the spirits above. So while the heavens rejoiced because God had mercy on Israel (Isaiah 44:23), and not only on Israel according to the flesh but also on the Israel understood according to the spirit, the foundations of the earth sounded the trumpet, that is, those who perform the sacred service of the gospel oracles. Their piercing sound was carried everywhere, and like sacred trumpets they cried aloud, proclaiming the Savior’s glory to people everywhere and calling to the knowledge of Christ both those of the circumcision and those who once worshiped the creation rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25).

For what reason do we say they are called the foundations of the earth? Christ is indeed the foundation of all and the unshakable base, who upholds all things and holds firm in well-being whatever has been set upon Him. For on Him we are all built up, a spiritual house (1 Peter 2:5), fitted together through the Spirit into a holy temple, into His dwelling place (Ephesians 2:20-22). For He dwells in our hearts through faith (Ephesians 3:17). But the apostles and evangelists may be understood as foundations nearer to Him and closer than we are, since they became eyewitnesses and ministers of the word (Luke 1:2), and became also a firm support for the faith. For when we recognize that we must follow their traditions, we shall keep our faith in Christ straight and undistorted.

For somewhere He said to the godly Peter, when Peter was wisely and blamelessly confessing his faith in Him and saying, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God” (Matthew 16:16): “You are Peter, and on this rock I will found My Church” (Matthew 16:18). By the rock, I think, He means the disciple’s unshakable firmness in faith. It is also said somewhere through the voice of the Psalmist: “His foundations are in the holy mountains” (Psalm 87:1). The holy apostles and evangelists may very fitly be compared to holy mountains; their knowledge has been laid like a foundation for those who came after them, and it does not let those whom they gathered in their net fall away into what is counterfeit in faith.

So the foundations of the earth sound the trumpet. But notice the exactness of the words. Moses was weak of voice and slow of tongue (Exodus 4:10), for the Law could be heard only by those in Judea. But sound the trumpet, you who are ambassadors for Christ (2 Corinthians 5:20)! “For their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world” (Psalm 19:4; Romans 10:18). He has commanded the mountains to shout for joy (Isaiah 44:23), here again calling the foundations of the earth mountains. For the godly disciples are admired and conspicuous, distinguished in deed and word, and to people everywhere …

choices.why: Septuagint Isaiah 44:23; Cyril reads the foundations as the apostles.

choices.english: holds firm in well-being whatever has been set upon Him
choices.why: Christ holds firm what rests on him; he is not 'holding together things that were falling'.
rejected: holding together the things that were falling
